codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUES: This payment processing module violates PCI DSS compliance by handling sensitive card data in plain text without encryption or tokenization. Card validation lacks Luhn algorithm checks, there's a Y2K bug in date parsing, no authentication controls, and no rate limiting on payment attempts. Additionally, all 7 functions lack test coverage, error handling is inconsistent, and configuration values are hard-coded. This code is NOT production-ready and requires substantial security remediation before deployment.

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL: Zero test coverage for 190 lines of critical payment processing code. This represents a severe risk for production deployment. Missing tests cover: (1) Payment Processing - no tests for the main flow, payment validation, or error scenarios; (2) Card Validation - no tests for expiry, CVV, Luhn algorithm, or format validation; (3) Pricing Logic - no tests for tax calculations, discounts, or currency precision; (4) Database Operations - no tests for transaction handling, concurrent access, or constraint violations; (5) Feature Access Control - no tests for subscription states, expiration, or tier validation; (6) Security - no PCI-DSS compliance testing or card data masking verification; (7) Edge Cases - missing tests for null inputs, invalid data, race conditions, and database failures. REQUIRED: Create src/premium.test.ts with minimum 150-200 test cases covering all 7 functions with 90%+ code coverage before production deployment.

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts module requires significant architectural refactoring. High-priority items include: (1) Implement tokenization service for card data handling (security-critical), (2) Extract database access into Repository/DAO pattern to eliminate query duplication, (3) Move hard-coded constants to centralized configuration module, (4) Replace string union types with enums for type safety, (5) Separate validation concerns into focused classes, (6) Implement consistent error handling strategy, (7) Add safe JSON parsing with error handling, (8) Implement caching layer for subscription lookups. These refactorings are essential for security compliance, maintainability, and testability before production deployment.

recommendations.description: Implement PCI-DSS compliant payment processing. Replace direct card handling with payment tokenization service (Stripe, Square, PayPal). Card data must never be transmitted or stored in plain text.
Add authentication and authorization checks to processPremiumPayment() to prevent privilege escalation attacks. Verify authenticated user matches userId parameter or has admin privileges.
Implement Luhn algorithm validation for credit card numbers. Current validation only checks length, allowing invalid card numbers to pass validation.

Create comprehensive test suite with minimum 150-200 test cases covering all 7 functions with 90%+ code coverage. Include unit tests for validation, pricing, database operations, and integration tests for payment flows.
Fix Y2K bug in expiry date parsing. Current implementation uses hardcoded 2000 offset which will fail for dates after 2099. Implement proper century windowing logic.
Implement Repository/DAO pattern to centralize database access and eliminate query duplication. Extract database operations into subscriptionRepository.ts with consistent error handling.

Extract all hard-coded constants (pricing, tax rates, card validation lengths, feature lists) to a centralized configuration module (src/config/subscriptionConfig.ts) for easier maintenance and updates.
Implement rate limiting on payment processing to prevent brute force attacks and fraud. Limit payment attempts per userId per time window with exponential backoff.
Add error handling for all database query failures. Wrap JSON.parse() calls in try-catch blocks. Implement custom error types (PaymentProcessingError) with appropriate error codes and retry logic.
Replace string union types ('premium' | 'enterprise') with TypeScript enums or const assertion types for improved type safety and refactoring support.
Implement idempotency key handling to prevent duplicate payments if requests are retried. Store idempotency_id with payment status in database and check for existing transactions before processing.

Implement dedicated validation classes (CardValidator) with separate methods for card number, CVV, and expiry date validation. Add Luhn algorithm implementation and format validation for all input types.
Add caching layer for subscription lookups (Redis or in-memory cache with TTL) to reduce database load. Implement batch query methods for multiple user lookups.
Add comprehensive JSDoc comments to all exported functions documenting parameters, return values, thrown errors, and important assumptions about timezone handling and subscription lifecycle.
